# planec — Plane API CLI & TypeScript Library

Typed HTTP client for [Plane API](https://plane.so). Zero runtime dependencies, ESM-only.

Package: `@gzl10/plane-client`
Install (library): `npm install @gzl10/plane-client`
Install (CLI): `npm install -g @gzl10/plane-client`

## TypeScript Library Usage

```typescript
import { PlaneClient, PlaneApiError } from '@gzl10/plane-client'

const client = new PlaneClient({
  baseUrl: 'https://plane.example.com',
  apiKey: 'pk_...',
  workspace: 'my-workspace',
})

// list() returns Page<WorkItem> with { items, hasNext, nextCursor?, total? }
const page = await client.workItems.list('project-uuid')
for (const item of page.items) console.log(item.name)

// get() returns WorkItem | null (null on 404, no error)
const workItem = await client.workItems.get('PROJ-42')

// listAll() yields AsyncIterable<WorkItem>, auto-pages through all results
for await (const item of client.workItems.listAll('project-uuid')) {
  console.log(item.name)
}
```

All resource classes follow the same pattern: `list()` → `Page<T>` (or `T[]` for the small
per-project collections), `get()` → `T | null`, `create()` → `T`, `update()` → `T`.
The `T[]` ones (`states`, `labels`, `cycles`, `modules`) walk every page internally; each also
exposes `listPage()` for one page and `listAll()` as an async iterable.

## Setup

```bash
planec config set baseUrl https://plane.example.com
echo "$PLANE_TOKEN" | planec login --token-stdin   # --token <value> also works, but see Secrets below
planec workspace use YOUR_WORKSPACE_SLUG   # optional — or use --workspace / PLANE_WORKSPACE
planec use PROJECT_UUID                    # optional — or use -p / PLANE_PROJECT
```

Config saved to `~/.planec/config.json`. View with `planec config show`.

## Context resolution

Workspace slug resolved in priority order:
1. `--workspace <slug>` global flag (before subcommand)
2. `PLANE_WORKSPACE=<slug>` environment variable
3. Active workspace saved via `planec workspace use <slug>`

Project UUID resolved in priority order:
1. `--project <uuid>` / `-p <uuid>` flag on any command
2. `PLANE_PROJECT=<uuid>` environment variable
3. Active project saved via `planec use <uuid>`

### Secrets

Pass the token on **stdin**, not in argv: `echo "$TOKEN" | planec login --token-stdin`, or
`planec config set apiKey --stdin`. An argument is readable in `ps` while the command runs, lands in
the shell history, and is echoed by any harness that logs the command line it ran. `--token <value>`
still works and warns on stderr. In a script, `PLANE_API_KEY` in the environment is the preferred
route and needs no `login` at all.

Credentials resolved in priority order:
1. `PLANE_BASE_URL` / `PLANE_API_KEY` environment variables
2. `baseUrl` / `apiKey` saved in `~/.planec/config.json`

The env wins so a single machine can hold several identities. The config file is read from
`os.homedir()`, so when several agents share one system user they also share one identity and every
work item they move is attributed to the same person. Exporting `PLANE_API_KEY` per process is the
only way to tell them apart.

Minimum required config: `baseUrl` + `apiKey` (login, or the env vars above). Workspace and project
can be passed inline:

```bash
planec --workspace my-slug --json work-items list -p <project-uuid>
PLANE_WORKSPACE=my-slug PLANE_PROJECT=<uuid> planec work-items list --json
```

## JSON output

All read commands accept `--json` for machine-readable output:

```bash
planec --json work-items list | jq '.items[].sequence_id'
planec work-items search "auth" --json | jq '.[] | {id, name, state}'
```

Every command accepts `--json`, including the ones whose only output is "it worked": those emit
`{"ok": true, ...}` instead of a sentence (`modules|cycles delete`, `add-work-items`,
`remove-work-item`, `cycles archive|transfer`, `intake accept|decline`, `comments delete`,
`attachments delete`, `projects delete`, `projects members deactivate`, `invitations delete`,
`config set|show`, `login`, `use`, `workspace use`).

`--json` output is flushed before exit, so piping large payloads to `jq` never
truncates. When a list returns zero results, the resolved `workspace=…, project=…`
context is printed to **stderr** (stdout stays clean) so an empty result caused by
the wrong context is not silent. `401`/`403` errors add an actionable hint on stderr.

## Reports (cross-workspace)

```
planec report work-items [--workspaces <slugs...>] [--status open|done|all] [--group backlog,started,...]
                         [--project PCL,NXI] [--assignee <uuid...>] [--since DATE] [--until DATE]
                         [--intake] [--intake-only] [--format table|json|csv|md] [--json]
```

The only non-project-scoped command group. `--status open` (the default) means
backlog+unstarted+started; `--group` overrides it with exact state groups.

**The workspace list is your input, not a discovery.** The v1 API has no route that lists
workspaces, so "every project I can see" is unreachable; the reachable version is "every project in
the workspaces I name". Save them once with `planec workspace add <slug>` (`workspace list` /
`workspace remove` manage it) and the flag becomes optional. Note the flag is `--workspaces`
(plural): `--workspace` is the global single-slug flag.

Grouping goes through `state.group`, never the state name — each project renames its states, so a
report keyed on names splits one column into three. Every filter runs client-side, because v1 ignores
`state`/`priority`/`assignees`/… on `/work-items/` and answers 400 to `pql`/`filters` on Community.
`fields=` is honoured and is what keeps the payload small; `per_page` is deliberately not sent, since
without it the endpoint returns every work item in a single response.

`--intake` **adds** the untriaged queue rather than filtering it: pending intake issues are already
absent from `/work-items/`, so what is missing is a way to see them, not a way to hide them.
Accepted ones are skipped — they are in the work item listing already.

A workspace **or a single project** that answers 403 is skipped with a stderr warning and the report
is marked `"partial": true`, with `"skipped": [...]` for workspaces and `"skippedProjects": [...]`
for projects — one unreadable project (an orphan, a disabled feature) does not take the sweep down.
If **every** workspace is refused the command fails with exit 1 instead of returning an empty report:
that pattern is the credential, not your permissions (typically a `PLANE_API_KEY` in the environment
overriding the config).

All the clients share one rate-limit state, because Plane throttles per API key and a sweep builds
one client per workspace.

The JSON of `report` is **camelCase** (`identifier`, `stateGroup`, `createdAt`), unlike every other
`--json` in the CLI, which is snake_case because it hands back the API's payload untouched. The
report is not an API payload: it is an object this client assembles (identifier rebuilt, state
resolved against the project's states, counts aggregated), so snake_case would suggest an origin it
does not have. Same shape from `buildWorkItemReport()` in the library.

Budget: 1 request per workspace + 2 per project (+1 per project with `--intake`). Measured: 10
requests for 741 work items across 3 projects.

## Rate limiting

Plane throttles per API key (`API_KEY_RATE_LIMIT`, default `60/minute`) and reports
`x-ratelimit-remaining` / `x-ratelimit-reset` on every response. The client paces itself against
those headers — it waits for the window to roll over when the quota is nearly spent — and honours
`Retry-After` on a 429. Configure with `rateLimit: { enabled, minRemaining, maxWaitMs }`; observe
with the `onThrottle` hook. An instance that sends no headers keeps the old blind-retry behaviour.

For a long sweep this means you no longer have to sleep defensively between requests: the client
knows how much quota is left and when it comes back.

Several clients on one API key (one per workspace, say) must share the quota, because Plane counts it
per key:

```ts
import { PlaneClient, createRateLimitState } from "@gzl10/plane-client";
const quota = createRateLimitState();
const clients = slugs.map((workspace) =>
  new PlaneClient({ baseUrl, apiKey, workspace, rateLimit: { quota } }));
```

## Reading a work item's state

`WorkItem.state` is a UUID on the bare endpoint and the full `State` object whenever the request asks
for `expand=state` — which every CLI read does. Narrow it with the exported helpers instead of
writing the `typeof` dance at each use site:

```ts
import { stateId, stateName, isExpandedState } from "@gzl10/plane-client";
stateId(item.state)     // always the UUID
stateName(item.state)   // the display name, or null if only a UUID is available
```

### states y labels — dos validaciones que la API no hace

- **`states create` exige `--group` aunque la API lo dé por opcional.** Plane acepta un estado sin
  grupo y lo archiva bajo **backlog** sin decir nada, así que un "En revisión" creado a la ligera
  cuenta como backlog en todos los conteos, filtros e informes. El grupo decide cómo se trata ese
  trabajo, no es decoración.
- **`--color` se valida como hex** (`#rgb` o `#rrggbb`) en labels y states. Plane guarda lo que le
  mandes: `--color verde` se aceptaba con 200 y quedaba almacenado tal cual, invisible hasta que el
  tablero lo renderiza. En `states create` el color es **obligatorio para la API** (400 sin él), así
  que el CLI pone un gris neutro por defecto.

### Validación local de flags

El CLI rechaza antes de salir a la red lo que la API ignora en silencio o castiga:

- `--order-by`: solo los 16 valores que Plane honra. Ojo con `name`, que **no** existe (hay
  `state__name`); la API lo descarta y devuelve un listado desordenado con aspecto de ordenado.
- `--per-page` / `--limit`: entero ≥ 1, y `--per-page` con tope 100. Un `-5` provocaba un **500** en
  el servidor; `0` y `abc` se descartaban y desactivaban la paginación devolviendo el proyecto entero.
- `--status` de módulos, `--group` de estados, `--priority`, `--type` de relations: enums cerrados.
- `--color`: hex.
- `report --since/--until`: además de cada fecha por separado, se comprueba que la ventana no esté
  invertida — devolvía `0 item(s)`, que se lee como "no hay trabajo" en vez de "cambiaste las fechas".

### Intake: dos ids, y la tabla imprime el que no vale

`intake list` muestra en su columna ID el id del **registro de intake**, no el del work item. Los
endpoints que escriben (`accept`, `decline`) y los de adjuntos van por el id del **issue**, y con el
otro responden 404. El cliente resuelve uno desde el otro (`intake.resolveIssueId`), así que los
comandos aceptan cualquiera de los dos: `intake accept <cualquiera>` y
`work-items attachments upload <cualquiera>` funcionan. Si llamas a la API a mano, la distinción
sigue siendo tuya.

`accept`/`decline` comprueban además que el estado devuelto sea el que pidieron, en vez de fiarse del
200.

## Concurrent writes: the API has no lost-update protection

Two `work-items update` calls on the **same** work item at the same time both answer `200`, each
confirming its own field, and one of the two changes is silently rolled back. Measured against 1.4.2:
three of five paired runs lost a field. Plane's PATCH is a read-modify-write over the snapshot it
read on entry, and there is nothing to guard with — work items expose no `version`, and no `ETag` or
`Last-Modified` comes back.

This matters here more than it would elsewhere, because the callers of this CLI are agents, and two
agents touching one work item is the normal case, not the exotic one.

- Serialise writes per work item. Different work items in parallel are fine.
- If a field matters, re-read after writing and compare. The write's own response is not evidence:
  it echoes what you asked for whether or not it survived.
- The response check that `intake accept` does cannot help here for that reason.

## Exit codes

```
0   success
1   failure, or the user declined a confirmation prompt
2   bad usage: unknown flag, missing argument, contradictory options
3   the named resource does not exist
4   credential missing, rejected, or not allowed here (401 and 403 alike)
```

A declined prompt exits **1**, so `planec projects delete X && next-step` no longer runs
`next-step` after an abort. A missing resource exits **3** and writes to stderr — stdout stays
empty, so `planec work-items get PROJ-999 --json | jq` fails instead of parsing a sentence. `4`
covers 401 and 403 together: to a script both mean "retrying will not help until the credential
changes". Flags are validated before any request, so a typo costs `2` and no round trip.

## Pagination

`work-items list` and `intake list` fetch **one page** and warn on stderr when more exist
(`Showing the first N of M …`). Pass `--all` to walk every page. Note `/work-items/` only paginates
when `per_page` is sent, so without `--per-page` the default call already returns everything in one
response.

## Commands

### Config & Auth
```
planec config set baseUrl <url>      Set Plane base URL
planec config set apiKey --stdin     Set API key from stdin (use login instead)
planec config show [--json]          Show effective config and which layer each value came from
planec login --token-stdin           Save API token, read from stdin (preferred)
planec login --token <token>         Same, but the secret sits in argv — deprecated, warns on stderr
planec use <uuid|IDENTIFIER>         Set active project (stores the resolved UUID)
planec workspace use <slug>          Set active workspace
planec workspace add <slug>          Add a workspace to the `report` sweep list
planec workspace remove <slug>       Remove one from that list
planec workspace list [--json]       Show the active workspace and the report list
```

All `-p/--project` flags accept a UUID **or** the project identifier (`-p PCL`); so do PLANE_PROJECT and `planec use PCL` (which stores the resolved UUID). A UUID costs no request; an identifier costs a project listing.
Identifier shape (verified against 1.4.1): alphanumerics and underscore, leading digit allowed (10TEST, A_B ok; A-B rejected by Plane).
Intake status codes: -2 pending, -1 declined, 0 snoozed, 1 accepted, 2 duplicate.

### Projects
```
planec projects list [--per-page n] [--json]   # workspace-level; NO -p flag — this is where the project UUID comes from
planec projects get <uuid|IDENTIFIER> [--json]
planec projects create --name "New" --identifier NEW [--description "..."] [--cycles] [--pages] [--no-modules] [--no-intake] [--no-views] [--json]
planec projects update <uuid|IDENTIFIER> [--name ...] [--identifier NEW] [--description ...] [--cycles|--no-cycles] [--modules|--no-modules] [--intake|--no-intake] [--views|--no-views] [--pages|--no-pages] [--yes] [--json]
planec projects delete <uuid|IDENTIFIER> [--confirm <IDENTIFIER>] [--dry-run]
```
create defaults: work items + modules + intake + views ON, cycles + pages OFF.
delete does NOT accept --yes: it prints what it cascades to and requires the identifier typed back (or --confirm <IDENTIFIER>).
update --identifier prompts before renaming the prefix (rewrites every PROJ-N reference) unless --yes.
Walks every page (the API defaults to 20 per page), so the listing is never silently truncated.
Table columns: identifier / name / uuid. `--json` gives the full raw project objects.

### Work Items
```
planec work-items list [-p uuid] [--order-by field] [--per-page n] [--expand fields] [--with-modules] [--all] [--json]   # --expand defaults to state,modules; --all walks every page
planec work-items get PROJ-42 [--with-modules] [--with-comments] [--json]                                        # requests expand=state,modules; always checks for comments (stderr hint), --with-comments attaches bodies
planec work-items get-by-id <uuid|PROJ-42> [-p uuid] [--with-modules] [--with-comments] [--json]
planec work-items search "query" [--workspace-search] [-p uuid] [--limit n] [--json]
planec work-items create [-p uuid] --name "title" [--priority urgent|high|medium|low|none] [--state uuid] [--labels uuid1,uuid2] [--assignee ivy,gonzalo] [--assignees uuid1] [--module uuid] [--description-html "<p>text</p>" | --description-html-file path.html] [--json]   # --module adds it to a module after creation
planec work-items update <uuid|PROJ-42> [-p uuid] [--name ...] [--priority ...] [--state ...] [--assignee ivy,gonzalo] [--description-html "<p>..." | --description-html-file path.html] [--json]

# --assignee takes names, emails or UUIDs and warns on stderr if the assignee is not an
# active project member (Plane answers 200 with assignees: [] in that case). --assignees
# is the older flag: raw UUIDs, unchecked. On update, --assignee REPLACES the whole set
# (it never merges); --assignee "" clears every assignee. The two flags are mutually exclusive.
planec work-items delete <uuid|PROJ-42> [-p uuid] [--yes] [--json]     # borrado permanente; pide confirmación sin --yes
planec work-items activities <uuid|PROJ-42> [-p uuid] [--json]        # tabla: fecha legible, verbo, campo y el cambio (old → new)
```

### Comments
```
planec work-items comments list <workItemId> [-p uuid] [--json]   # fecha legible, autor, y el CUERPO del comentario
planec work-items comments create <workItemId> --comment-html "<p>text</p>" [-p uuid] [--json]
planec work-items comments update <workItemId> <commentId> --comment-html "<p>text</p>" [-p uuid]
planec work-items comments delete <workItemId> <commentId> [-p uuid] [--yes]
```

### Links & Relations
```
planec work-items links create <workItemId> --url https://... [--title "title"] [-p uuid]
planec work-items links list <workItemId> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec work-items links update <workItemId> <linkId> [--url ...] [--title ...] [-p uuid] [--json]   # hace merge: --title solo no borra la url
planec work-items links delete <workItemId> <linkId> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec work-items relations list <workItemId> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec work-items relations create <workItemId> --type blocking --issues PROJ-43,PROJ-44 [-p uuid]   # refs: UUIDs or PROJ-N; comma- or space-separated
```

### Cycles (Sprints)
```
planec cycles list [-p uuid] [--json]
planec cycles get <id> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec cycles create [-p uuid] --name "Sprint 1" [--start-date 2026-01-01] [--end-date 2026-01-14] [--json]
planec cycles update <id> [-p uuid] [--name ...] [--start-date ...] [--end-date ...] [--json]
planec cycles archive <id> [-p uuid]
planec cycles transfer <fromId> --to <toId> [-p uuid]
planec cycles work-items <id> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec cycles add-work-items <cycleId> --work-items PROJ-42,PROJ-43 [-p uuid]   # refs: UUIDs or PROJ-N
planec cycles remove-work-item <cycleId> <workItemId|PROJ-42> [-p uuid]
planec cycles delete <id> [-p uuid] [--yes]           # prompts unless --yes
```

### Modules
```
planec modules list [-p uuid] [--json]
planec modules get <id> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec modules create [-p uuid] --name "Module 1" [--start-date ...] [--target-date ...] [--json]
planec modules update <id> [-p uuid] [--name ...] [--status ...] [--json]
planec modules work-items <id> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec modules add-work-items <moduleId> --work-items PROJ-42,PROJ-43 [-p uuid]   # refs: UUIDs or PROJ-N
planec modules remove-work-item <moduleId> <workItemId|PROJ-42> [-p uuid]
planec modules delete <id> [-p uuid] [--yes]          # prompts unless --yes
```

### Members, Project Membership, Invitations
```
planec members list [--json]                                          # workspace members: role, is_active, user UUID
planec projects members list [-p uuid|IDENTIFIER] [--json]            # project members with project role + is_active
planec projects members add [-p uuid] --member ivy[,codex] [--role admin|member|guest] [--json]   # name, email or UUID; defaults to member (the API itself defaults to guest)
planec projects members set-role <membershipId> [-p uuid] --role admin|member|guest [--json]
planec projects members deactivate <membershipId> [-p uuid] [--yes]
planec invitations list [--json]
planec invitations create <email> [--role admin|member|guest] [--json]
planec invitations set-role <invitationId> --role admin|member|guest [--json]
planec invitations delete <invitationId> [--yes]
```

Requires **Plane 1.4.1+** (the `-lite` endpoints) and a **workspace-admin token**: Plane gates every
member listing behind workspace-admin, so a lower role gets 403 here and on `--assignee <name>` — use
`--assignees <uuid>` in that case.

`<membershipId>` is the ProjectMember id, and API v1 reveals it ONLY in the
response of `projects members add` — no listing carries it (both listings return
the *user* id). Keep it if you plan to change the role later.

Roles are `admin` (20), `member` (15), `guest` (5). Nothing else is valid.

### States, Labels, Intake
```
planec states list [-p uuid] [--json]
planec states get <id> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec states create --name "En revisión" --group started [--color "#ff0000"] [--description ...] [-p uuid] [--json]
planec states update <id> [--name ...] [--group ...] [--color ...] [--description ...] [-p uuid] [--json]
planec states delete <id> [-p uuid] [--yes] [--json]
planec labels list [-p uuid] [--json]
planec labels create [-p uuid] --name "bug" [--color "#ff0000"] [--json]
planec labels get <id> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec labels update <id> [--name ...] [--color ...] [-p uuid] [--json]
planec labels delete <id> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec intake list [-p uuid|IDENTIFIER] [--all] [--json]   # table shows issue_detail.name + labelled status; --json stays raw
planec intake create [-p uuid] --name "Bug report" [--priority medium] [--description-html "<p>..." | --description-html-file path.html] [--json]
planec intake accept <id> [-p uuid]     # <id> = intake record id (as listed) or work item id
planec intake decline <id> [-p uuid]
```

### Attachments

```
planec work-items attachments list <workItemId> [-p uuid] [--json]
planec work-items attachments upload <workItemId> --file ./report.pdf [--type application/pdf] [--name report.pdf] [-p uuid] [--json]   # drives the full presigned-URL flow in one call
planec work-items attachments download-url <workItemId> <attachmentId> [-p uuid] [--json]   # prints the presigned S3 URL (the detail GET redirects, it does not return JSON)
planec work-items attachments delete <workItemId> <attachmentId> [-p uuid]
```

`workItemId` accepts a `PROJ-42` identifier, a work item UUID, or an intake
issue's underlying `issue` UUID (from `intake list`) — attachments live on the
same `Issue` record either way, there is no separate intake-attachments endpoint.

## Non-interactive use (cron, CI, agents)

Destructive commands ask for confirmation on stderr. With **no terminal** (stdin closed, cron, an agent)
they now REFUSE with a clear error instead of hanging:

```
Refusing to prompt: stdin is not a terminal. Pass --yes to run non-interactively.
```

Pass `--yes` (`modules delete`, `cycles delete`, `projects members deactivate`, `invitations delete`,
`projects update --identifier`) or `--confirm <IDENTIFIER>` (`projects delete`, which never takes a bare
`--yes`). Before 0.18.0 these hung until Node killed them with exit 13.

## Identifiers vs UUIDs

```
PROJ-42   → human-readable sequence ID (use: work-items get PROJ-42)
uuid      → internal UUID (use: work-items get-by-id <uuid> -p <project-uuid>)
```

The CLI accepts EITHER a `PROJ-42` identifier or a UUID for `work-items update`,
`get-by-id`, `activities`, `comments`, `links`, `relations`, and
`modules/cycles remove-work-item` — an identifier is resolved to its UUID
automatically before hitting the UUID-only endpoint. The TypeScript library's
`update`/`getById`/etc. still take a UUID directly.

## Typical agent workflow

```bash
# 1. Discover work items
planec --json work-items search "authentication" | jq '.[] | {id: .sequence_id, name}'

# 2. Get by human-readable ID
planec --json work-items get PROJ-42

# 3. Create new work item
planec --json work-items create -p $PROJECT --name "Fix login" --priority high

# 4. Move to active cycle
planec cycles list -p $PROJECT --json | jq '.[0].id' > /tmp/cycle_id
planec cycles add-work-items $(cat /tmp/cycle_id) --work-items $WORK_ITEM_UUID -p $PROJECT
```

## API v1 Gotchas (CRITICAL)

Work items list DOES NOT filter by state/priority/labels — these query params are silently ignored. Use:
- `search` endpoint (textual, workspace-level)
- `/cycles/{id}/work-items/` or `/modules/{id}/work-items/` (scoped)
- `listAll()` + filter locally

Pages API not available in v1 — no `planec pages` command.
Views API not available in v1 — no `planec views` command.
Rate limit is aggressive (~3s between bulk operations recommended).
Project `network` (visibility) is accepted and SILENTLY DISCARDED on create and update — not settable via API v1, only in the UI.
`intake_view: true` in a project POST stores the flag but does not provision the queue: the first intake call answers 500. A PATCH with the same value fixes it (projects.create() does this).
Project names are unique per workspace: a repeat gives 409 {"name":"The project name is already taken"}.
Deleting a project CASCADES to its work items, modules, cycles and intake, with no warning. An orphaned cycle answers 403, not 404.
The auth header is case-sensitive on the wire: send exactly `X-API-Key`. A client that normalises it to `X-Api-Key` (e.g. Python's `urllib.request`) gets **403 on every workspace**, which reads as a permissions problem but is not.
Workspace roles are READ-ONLY in v1: `/workspaces/{slug}/members/` is GET-only. No role change, no removal. New members only via `invitations`.
The ProjectMember id needed by `set-role`/`deactivate` is NOT discoverable: no listing returns it, only the POST that created the membership does. A GET with the user id answers 404.
Deleting a project member does NOT remove it: `DELETE` sets `is_active=false` and answers 204, the flat `/members/` endpoint keeps listing it, re-adding answers 400 "The payload is not valid", and `PATCH {"is_active": true}` answers 200 while changing nothing. Reactivation requires the Plane UI. Use `/project-members-lite/` to see the real `is_active`.
Assigning a user who is not an active project member is accepted and DROPPED: 200 with `assignees: []`.
`POST .../members/` without `role` creates a GUEST (5). The body shape is `{member, role}` — `{members:[{member_id,role}]}` answers 400.
Invitations do NOT send an email in v1 (the UI does) and do NOT check whether the address is already a member (201 either way).
The two member listings disagree: `/members/` is a flat array without `is_active` that ignores `per_page`; `/members-lite/` and `/project-members-lite/` are paginated and carry `role` + `is_active`. This client uses the -lite ones.
EVERY list endpoint returns `next_cursor` even on the last page (`next_page_results: false`, and that cursor returns `count: 0` with yet another cursor behind it). Pagination must stop on `next_page_results`, never on the cursor being present — doing otherwise loops for ever on empty pages until the API answers 429. Fixed in 0.18.0 for work items, cycles and modules (projects since 0.14.0).

## TypeScript API Reference

### PlaneClient

```typescript
class PlaneClient {
  constructor(config: { baseUrl: string; apiKey: string; workspace: string; timeout?: number; retry?: { maxRetries?: number; retryOn?: number[] }; onRequest?: (req: { method: string; url: string }) => void; onResponse?: (res: { method: string; url: string; status: number; durationMs: number }) => void })
  version(): Promise<string>
  workItems: WorkItemsResource
  projects: ProjectsResource
  states: StatesResource
  labels: LabelsResource
  modules: ModulesResource
  cycles: CyclesResource
  intake: IntakeResource
}
```

### Resources — Common CRUD Pattern

Every resource follows the same method signatures:

```typescript
list(projectId: string, options?: ListOptions): Promise<Page<T>>      // Paginated results
get(identifier: string): Promise<T | null>                             // Returns null on 404
create(projectId: string, input: CreateInput): Promise<T>              // Creates and returns the resource
update(projectId: string, id: string, input: UpdateInput): Promise<T>  // Updates and returns the resource
listAll(projectId: string, options?: Omit<ListOptions, 'cursor'>): AsyncIterable<T>  // Yields all items
```

### Resource-specific methods

```typescript
// WorkItemsResource
workItems.list(projectId, options?: { orderBy?: string; fields?: string[]; expand?: string[] }): Promise<Page<WorkItem>>
workItems.get(identifier: 'PROJ-42'): Promise<WorkItem | null>

workItems.search({ query, limit?, workspaceSearch?, projectId? }): Promise<WorkItemSearchResult[]>

workItems.comments.list(projectId, workItemId): Promise<Comment[]>

workItems.comments.update(projectId, workItemId, commentId, { commentHtml }): Promise<Comment>
workItems.comments.delete(projectId, workItemId, commentId): Promise<void>
workItems.links.create(projectId, workItemId, { url, title? }): Promise<unknown>
workItems.relations.list(projectId, workItemId): Promise<Record<RelationType, string[]>>
workItems.relations.create(projectId, workItemId, { relationType, issues }): Promise<RelationItem[]>
workItems.activities.list(projectId, workItemId, options?): Promise<Page<Activity>>

// MembersResource (workspace-level, read-only — v1 exposes no writes)
members.list(options?): Promise<Page<WorkspaceMember>>          // backed by /members-lite/ (paginated, has role + is_active)
members.listAll(options?): AsyncIterable<WorkspaceMember>
members.find(ref: string): Promise<WorkspaceMember | null>      // by display name, email or UUID
members.resolve(ref: string): Promise<string>                   // → user UUID for assignees; throws if no match
members.resolveMany(refs: string[]): Promise<string[]>          // one listing for the whole batch

// ProjectMembersResource
projectMembers.list(projectId, options?): Promise<Page<ProjectMember>>   // backed by /project-members-lite/
projectMembers.listAll(projectId, options?): AsyncIterable<ProjectMember>
projectMembers.add(projectId, userId, role = Role.Member): Promise<ProjectMembership>   // the returned id is the ONLY handle to the row
projectMembers.updateRole(projectId, membershipId, role): Promise<ProjectMembership>    // membershipId from add(), NOT the user id
projectMembers.deactivate(projectId, membershipId): Promise<void>                       // Plane's DELETE: is_active=false, one-way

// InvitationsResource (workspace-level)
invitations.list(): Promise<WorkspaceInvitation[]>   // flat array, not paginated
invitations.get(id): Promise<WorkspaceInvitation | null>
invitations.create({ email, role? }): Promise<WorkspaceInvitation>   // sends NO email in v1
invitations.updateRole(id, role): Promise<WorkspaceInvitation>       // email cannot be changed
invitations.delete(id): Promise<void>                                // refused once accepted

// CyclesResource
cycles.list(projectId): Promise<Page<Cycle>>
cycles.get(id): Promise<Cycle | null>
cycles.create(projectId, { name, description?, start_date?, end_date? }): Promise<Cycle>
cycles.update(projectId, id, { name?, description?, start_date?, end_date? }): Promise<Cycle>
cycles.delete(projectId, cycleId): Promise<void>
cycles.archive(projectId, id): Promise<void>
cycles.transfer(projectId, fromId, { to: toId }): Promise<Cycle>
cycles.workItems(projectId, cycleId): Promise<Page<WorkItem>>
cycles.workItemsAll(projectId, cycleId): AsyncIterable<WorkItem>
cycles.addWorkItems(projectId, cycleId, { workItems: string[] }): Promise<void>
cycles.removeWorkItem(projectId, cycleId, workItemId): Promise<void>

// ModulesResource
modules.list(projectId): Promise<Page<Module>>
modules.get(id): Promise<Module | null>
modules.create(projectId, { name, description?, start_date?, target_date? }): Promise<Module>
modules.update(projectId, id, { name?, description?, status?, start_date?, target_date? }): Promise<Module>
modules.delete(projectId, moduleId): Promise<void>
modules.workItems(projectId, moduleId): Promise<Page<WorkItem>>
modules.workItemsAll(projectId, moduleId): AsyncIterable<WorkItem>
modules.addWorkItems(projectId, moduleId, { workItems: string[] }): Promise<void>
modules.removeWorkItem(projectId, moduleId, workItemId): Promise<void>
modules.membershipMap(projectId): Promise<Map<string, Module[]>>   // client-side workaround, see below
attachModules(items, membership): T[]                              // merges membershipMap into work items (pure fn, exported from resources/modules)

// ProjectsResource (workspace-level — no projectId argument)
projects.list(options?: { perPage?, cursor?, signal? }): Promise<Page<Project>>   // perPage clamped to 100 (API max)
projects.listAll(options?: { perPage?, signal? }): AsyncIterable<Project>
projects.get(projectId): Promise<Project | null>                                 // null on 404
projects.create(input: CreateProjectInput): Promise<Project>                     // POST + follow-up PATCH for the toggles
projects.update(projectId, input: UpdateProjectInput): Promise<Project>
projects.delete(projectId): Promise<void>                                        // CASCADES

// States, Labels, Intake (non-paginated)
states.list(projectId): Promise<State[]>
labels.list(projectId): Promise<Label[]>
labels.create(projectId, { name, color? }): Promise<Label>
intake.list(projectId): Promise<IntakeIssue[]>
intake.create(projectId, { name, description_html?, priority? }): Promise<IntakeIssue>
intake.accept(projectId, id): Promise<IntakeIssue>
intake.decline(projectId, id): Promise<IntakeIssue>

// AttachmentsResource (mounted as workItems.attachments — also covers intake work items, same underlying issue id)
workItems.attachments.list(projectId, workItemId): Promise<Attachment[]>
workItems.attachments.upload(projectId, workItemId, { name, type?, size, externalId?, externalSource? }, fileData: Uint8Array): Promise<Attachment>   // full 3-step flow: credentials -> S3 POST -> confirm
workItems.attachments.getDownloadUrl(projectId, workItemId, attachmentId): Promise<string>   // resolves the presigned S3 URL; the detail GET is a redirect, not JSON
workItems.attachments.delete(projectId, workItemId, attachmentId): Promise<void>
```

### Page<T>

```typescript
interface Page<T> {
  items: T[]
  total?: number
  nextCursor?: string
  hasNext: boolean
}
```

### PlaneApiError

```typescript
class PlaneApiError extends Error {
  status: number
  statusText: string
  code?: string
  body?: unknown
  isAuth: boolean       // true if status === 401
  isPermission: boolean // true if status === 403
  isNotFound: boolean   // true if status === 404
  isRateLimit: boolean  // true if status === 429
  isTimeout: boolean    // true if status === 408
}
```

### Exported Types

```typescript
type Priority = "urgent" | "high" | "medium" | "low" | "none"
type StateGroup = "backlog" | "unstarted" | "started" | "completed" | "cancelled"
type RelationType = "blocking" | "blocked_by" | "duplicate" | "relates_to" | "start_before" | "start_after" | "finish_before" | "finish_after"
type RelationsMap = Record<RelationType, string[]>

interface WorkItem { id: string; name: string; sequence_id: number; state: string; priority: Priority; assignees: string[]; labels: string[]; parent?: string; created_at: string; updated_at: string; [key: string]: unknown }
interface Comment { id: string; comment_html: string; created_at: string; updated_at: string; [key: string]: unknown }
interface Activity { id: string; created_at: string; verb: string; field: string | null; old_value: string | null; new_value: string | null; comment: string | null; actor: string; [key: string]: unknown }
interface CreateProjectInput { name: string; identifier: string; description?: string; project_lead?: string; default_assignee?: string; timezone?: string; cycleView?: boolean; moduleView?: boolean; intakeView?: boolean; viewsView?: boolean; pageView?: boolean }
type UpdateProjectInput = Partial<CreateProjectInput>
interface Project { id: string; name: string; identifier: string; description?: string; network?: number; workspace?: string; project_lead?: string | null; [key: string]: unknown }
interface State { id: string; name: string; group: StateGroup; color: string; [key: string]: unknown }
interface Label { id: string; name: string; color?: string; [key: string]: unknown }
interface Module { id: string; name: string; description?: string; status?: string; start_date?: string; target_date?: string; [key: string]: unknown }
interface Cycle { id: string; name: string; description?: string; start_date?: string; end_date?: string; [key: string]: unknown }
interface CreateWorkItemInput { name: string; description_html?: string; state?: string; priority?: Priority; assignees?: string[]; labels?: string[]; parent?: string; start_date?: string; target_date?: string; estimate_point?: string | null; type?: string; module?: string }
interface UpdateWorkItemInput { name?: string; description_html?: string; state?: string; priority?: Priority; assignees?: string[]; labels?: string[]; start_date?: string; target_date?: string; estimate_point?: string | null; type?: string; module?: string }
interface WorkspaceMember { id: string; email: string; display_name: string; role: RoleValue; is_active: boolean; is_bot: boolean; [key: string]: unknown }   // id is the USER id (what assignees takes)
interface ProjectMember extends WorkspaceMember {}
interface ProjectMembership { id: string; member: string; role: RoleValue }   // id is the MEMBERSHIP id, only ever returned by add()
interface WorkspaceInvitation { id: string; email: string; role: RoleValue; accepted: boolean; responded_at?: string | null; [key: string]: unknown }
interface CreateInvitationInput { email: string; role?: RoleValue | RoleName }
const Role = { Admin: 20, Member: 15, Guest: 5 }   // the only values the API accepts
type RoleValue = 20 | 15 | 5
type RoleName = "admin" | "member" | "guest"
parseRole(role: RoleValue | RoleName | number | string): RoleValue   // throws on anything else
roleName(role: number): string
interface UpdateCommentInput { commentHtml: string }
interface CreateLinkInput { url: string; title?: string }
interface CreateRelationInput { relationType: RelationType; issues: string[] }
interface RelationItem { id: string; name: string; sequence_id: number; [key: string]: unknown }
```

## What This Does NOT Do

- **No OAuth** — Only API key authentication (`X-API-Key` header)
- **No Pages API** — Plane v1 does not expose pages via API key auth. `PagesResource` exists in source but is not mounted on `PlaneClient`.
- **No Views API** — Plane v1 does not expose views via API key auth.
- **No Sub-issues** — The `parent` field on WorkItem works (read/write), but `/work-items/{id}/sub-issues/` is not mounted in v1.
- **No external OAuth providers** — Google, GitHub, etc. login flows are not supported.
- **No webhooks** — Webhook creation/management is not exposed.
- **No workspace role management** — `/workspaces/{slug}/members/` is GET-only in v1: roles cannot be changed and members cannot be removed. Adding someone goes through `invitations` (which sends no email).
- **No removing a project member** — Plane's `DELETE` only deactivates (`is_active=false`), the flat listing keeps showing them, and neither re-adding nor `is_active: true` works. Reactivation is UI-only, so the method is named `deactivate()`.
- **`expand=modules` returns nothing** — A work item's module membership is not expanded by the v1 API (verified against Plane 1.4.1), so an empty `modules` field does NOT mean the item has no module. Check from the module side: `planec modules work-items <moduleId> -p <project>`, or pass `--with-modules` to `work-items list|get|get-by-id` (client-side workaround: walks every module in the project and cross-references — costs 1 extra request per module, so it's opt-in, not the default).
- **`work-items get`/`get-by-id` never include comments** — Comments are a separate resource (`GET .../comments/`); the item response has no count or preview of them. `get`/`get-by-id` now (≥0.12.0) always fetch the comment list as a side effect and print an stderr hint (`N comment(s) on <id> — ...`) if any exist — one extra request, cheap enough to be unconditional (unlike `--with-modules`). Pass `--with-comments` to attach the comment bodies to the JSON output instead of just the hint.
- **Plane rewrites description HTML on save** — The editor re-serialises what you send (injected `class`/`spellcheck` on `<code>`, adjacent tags reordered), so a `get` → string-replace → `update` round trip will not match on markup. Match on plain text, or append instead of editing in place.
- **A large description must go through `--description-html-file`** — Passing ~100 KB of HTML inline dies with `E2BIG` at the argv limit, before Plane ever sees it.
- **The attachment detail GET is a redirect, not a JSON endpoint** — `GET .../attachments/{id}/` 302-redirects to a presigned S3 URL (verified against Plane's public source, `IssueAttachmentDetailAPIEndpoint.get`); it does not return the attachment's metadata. `getDownloadUrl()` follows this manually (`redirect: "manual"`) and returns the `Location` header. Metadata comes from `list()` instead.
- **`attachments.list()` returns a plain array, not `{ results: [...] }`** — unlike every paginated resource in this client, the API returns `IssueAttachmentSerializer(many=True).data` directly (confirmed in source). The client handles both shapes defensively but there is no pagination here.
- **Attachments work on intake work items too** — intake issues are regular `Issue` rows under the hood; resolve the intake record to its `issue` UUID (`intake.resolveIssueId` / `intake list`) and use the same `workItems.attachments.*` methods. There is no separate intake-attachments endpoint.

## Error Handling Pattern

```typescript
import { PlaneApiError } from '@gzl10/plane-client'

try {
  await client.workItems.create('proj', { name: '' })
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof PlaneApiError) {
    if (err.isAuth) { /* invalid/expired API key */ }
    if (err.isPermission) { /* API key lacks permission */ }
    if (err.isNotFound) { /* should not happen — get() returns null */ }
    if (err.isRateLimit) { /* throttle requests */ }
    if (err.isTimeout) { /* increase timeout or retry */ }
  }
}
```

## Common Errors

```
baseUrl not configured         → planec config set baseUrl https://...
apiKey not configured          → planec login --token YOUR_KEY
workspace not configured       → planec workspace use YOUR_SLUG
No project specified           → planec use UUID  or  -p UUID  or  PLANE_PROJECT=UUID
Invalid project UUID           → UUID must match xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```
